svg.text: Four kinds of storage, each kept safe by its own rule
All of them are checked at compile time, with no lifetime annotations
own
Id<@a> (a 4-byte value)
read and written by index (@fb[y][x])
Values and second-class references (per call)
Holds: locals, struct values, parameter references
e.g. fn f(t: &Task) / if let Some(p) = @a.get(id)
Guarantee: references cannot be stored (F0515)
Freed: when the function or block ends
own regions (ownership trees)
Holds: a tree of own T; children packed into the parent
e.g. ok: own Button / win: Option<own Window>
Guarantee: one owner, move only (F0382)
Freed: the whole tree at once with its owner
Arenas (static tables in .bss)
Holds: tables like task_struct; links are Ids
e.g. arena @process: Process[64];
Guarantee: colouring (F2101), stale Id gives None
Freed: free bumps the generation (old Ids die)
Fixed-address regions (MMIO / VRAM)
Holds: the framebuffer and device registers
Guarantee: shape is the type, bounds at compile time
Freed: never (it is hardware)
Generated C: the only pointers stored in structs are own; links are uint32_t Ids; VRAM is a constant address + index
